events.body: I write regarding order BP-8676, delivered at 17:55 today. There are three matters. First, two 2-litre bottles of apple juice were packed on top of four bags of crisps, which are crushed. Second, I was charged for six carrier bags, having selected bagless delivery. Third, and of greater concern, a box of loose washing powder was placed in the same bag as a tub of ice cream and a block of cheddar. The box has split. There is powder over both items and inside the rim of the ice cream lid. I have set those two items aside in the bag, uneaten, and photographed them. I should be grateful if this were dealt with properly.

Order BP-8676 / DL-5289, delivered 17:55 today. The recipient reports: four bags of crisps crushed under juice bottles; six carrier bags charged on a bagless order; and a split box of loose washing powder in the same bag as a tub of ice cream and a block of cheddar, with powder on both and inside the ice cream lid rim. She has set those two items aside uneaten and has photos. Please advise who handles each point.

BP-8676: crisps x4 credited as damaged, done at our end, she will get the confirmation by email tonight. The bag charge is not ours, that is the Refunds team. The powder on the food items: we do not assess anything where a non-food product has been in contact with food. That goes to the Food-safety lead on the Safety incident queue. They decide what the customer is told about those items and they log the packing fault. We have not passed it on, we have no access to that queue.

I have received an email crediting the crisps. Thank you. It makes no mention of the washing powder, which I regard as the substantive issue. The cheddar is in its sealed wrapper and the ice cream lid was on. May I rinse the wrapper and use the cheese? And is the ice cream safe if I remove the top layer? I would rather not waste food unnecessarily, but I should like a clear answer this evening. The matter of the bag charge also remains.

I've attached the photo as photo-evidence-627.txt.
